title: Normalized point-dual evaluation and its coefficient transport
statement:
Fix the Poincare coefficient conventions [def-pod-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Write $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Use the point categories and $F_\Lambda=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and derived tensor and internal Hom [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $Q_s$ be finite reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ with $1\le m\le n$, integral reduction $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, completed integral scalar extension for a finite coefficient-field extension, rationalization, or extension at a common finite coefficient-field stage. Write $\Lambda'$ for its target coefficient ring and $q$ for the corresponding coefficient-module functor.
Let $C\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, let $u_\Lambda:\omega_{s,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$ be the identity-adjunction normalization, and set $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,\Lambda})$, $c=F_\Lambda C$, $d=F_\Lambda(D_sC)$. Write $j_{\Lambda,C}:d\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)=c^\vee$ for the specified point-duality map [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]. Let $\mu_\Lambda:d\otimes^Lc\xrightarrow{\sim}F_\Lambda(D_sC\otimes^LC)$ be the inverse fibre tensor comparison [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], and define
$$e_{\Lambda,C}=F_\Lambda(u_\Lambda\circ\operatorname{ev}_C)\circ\mu_\Lambda:d\otimes^Lc\to\Lambda,$$
using the fibre unit comparison. Then the actual specified $j$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{ev}_c\circ(j_{\Lambda,C}\otimes1_c)=e_{\Lambda,C}.$$
This normalization holds for the signed Hom-complex evaluation [def-pur-hom-complex], for completed integral tensor, and after rationalization and passage to a common finite field. In the order with the Hom factor first a degree-$r$ family $f$ evaluates on a section $x$ as $u_\Lambda(f(x))$, with Hom differential $df-(-1)^rfd$; when the factors are interchanged use the symmetry constraint.
Use the specified comparisons $t_{Q,B}$, their domains, and $\delta_{Q,C}$ of [lem-pod-point-dual-coefficient-domains]. Write $c'=F_{\Lambda'}Q_sC$, $d'=F_{\Lambda'}D_s(Q_sC)$, and define $e_{\Lambda',Q_sC}$ by the same formula, with its corresponding evaluation normalization for $j_{\Lambda',Q_sC}$. Let $\nu_q:qd\otimes^Lqc\xrightarrow{\sim}q(d\otimes^Lc)$ be the coefficient tensor constraint, with the coefficient unit identified with $\Lambda'$. Then the following equality of derived pairings holds:
$$e_{\Lambda',Q_sC}\circ\bigl((F_{\Lambda'}(\delta_{Q,C})\circ t_{Q,D_sC})\otimes t_{Q,C}\bigr)=q(e_{\Lambda,C})\circ\nu_q.$$
The internal-Hom comparison in this formula is the canonical evaluation transpose: if $\nu_{Q_s}:Q_sD_sC\otimes^LQ_sC\to Q_s(D_sC\otimes^LC)$ is the coefficient tensor constraint, its defining identity, including the dualizing comparison, is
$$\operatorname{ev}_{Q_sC}\circ(\delta_{Q,C}\otimes1)=Q_s(\operatorname{ev}_C)\circ\nu_{Q_s},$$
where the right side is followed by $Q_s\omega_{s,\Lambda}\cong\omega_{s,\Lambda'}$. All equalities use the prescribed comparisons, rather than arbitrary objectwise isomorphisms.

proof.text: Put $F=F_\Lambda$, $F'=F_{\Lambda'}$ and $A=D_sC$. By [lem-pod-point-dual-coefficient-domains], $A$, $Q_sC$ and $D_sQ_sC$ are in the required bounded constructible finite-Tor categories. Thus all displayed evaluations and $t_{Q,A},t_{Q,C}$ are defined. That node supplies naturality of $t$, its tensor and unit compatibility, and the normalization of $\delta_{Q,C}$. The tensor comparisons below are precisely those of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor].

source.place: second paragraph: domains and specified tensor/unit comparisons

proof.text:
First take $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ or $\mathcal O_E$. Write $H=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s)$ and $\rho=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,u_\Lambda)$. By [lem-pod-point-integral-evaluation-normalization], $j=\kappa\circ F\rho$, where $\kappa:FH\to c^\vee$ is the transpose of the actual sections evaluation through the specified tensor and unit maps, including completed tensor integrally. Uncurrying [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws], and using naturality of the tensor comparison, gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_c(j\otimes1)=F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,\Lambda_s})\mu_{H,C}(F\rho\otimes1)=F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,\Lambda_s}(\rho\otimes1))\mu_{A,C}=F(u_\Lambda\operatorname{ev}_{C,\omega})\mu_{A,C}=e_{\Lambda,C}.$$
The middle evaluation identity is postcomposition: on Hom-first representatives both sides send $f\otimes x$ to $u_\Lambda(f(x))$. In the input-first order the cited normalization gives $(-1)^{pr}$ on degrees $p,r$; the Koszul symmetry contributes the same sign, so the Hom-first formula has none. The differential [def-pur-hom-complex] verifies the chain identity explicitly:
$$(df)(x)+(-1)^r f(dx)=d(f(x)),\qquad df=d f-(-1)^r f d.$$
Postcomposition with the chain map $u_\Lambda$ preserves this identity.

source.place: second paragraph: normalized point evaluation; finite and completed integral stages

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [lem-pod-point-field-evaluation-normalization] supplies the same factorization $j=\kappa\circ F\rho$, with $\kappa$ the transpose of the actual evaluation, and the same signed convention. Hence the identical uncurrying calculation of step 2 proves $\operatorname{ev}_c(j\otimes1)=e_{\Lambda,C}$. Its representative-independent rational and common-stage comparisons ensure this is the specified $j$, including torsion integral representatives. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, choose a common finite coefficient field for the finitely many objects and arrows in the calculation; equality there gives equality of the represented arrows by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Applying steps 2 and 3 also to $Q_sC$ gives the required target normalization.

source.place: second paragraph: rational and common finite-field evaluation normalization

proof.text:
Let $w:Q_s\omega_{s,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{s,\Lambda'}$ be the dualizing comparison fixed by [lem-pod-point-dual-coefficient-domains], so $u_{\Lambda'}w=Q_su_\Lambda$ after the unit identification. That node defines $\delta_{Q,C}$ as the transpose of $w\,Q_s(\operatorname{ev}_C)
u_{Q_s}$. Uncurrying [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] gives exactly
$$\operatorname{ev}_{Q_sC}(\delta_{Q,C}\otimes1)=w\,Q_s(\operatorname{ev}_C)
u_{Q_s}.$$
Postcomposing with $u_{\Lambda'}$ yields $u_{\Lambda'}\operatorname{ev}_{Q_sC}(\delta\otimes1)=Q_s(u_\Lambda\operatorname{ev}_C)
u_{Q_s}$. This proves the claimed defining identity with its explicitly stated dualizing comparison.

source.place: second paragraph: coefficient internal-Hom comparison is the evaluation transpose

proof.text:
Set $v=u_\Lambda\operatorname{ev}_C:A\otimes^LC\to\Lambda_s$, $v'=u_{\Lambda'}\operatorname{ev}_{Q_sC}$, and abbreviate $t_{Q,B}$ to $t_B$. Naturality of the fibre tensor map and step 4 give
$$e'((F'\delta\,t_A)\otimes t_C)=F'(Q_sv)\,F'(\nu_{Q_s})\,\mu'_{Q_sA,Q_sC}(t_A\otimes t_C).$$
The tensor compatibility stated in [lem-pod-point-dual-coefficient-domains], with the orientations fixed by [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], is
$$F'(\nu_{Q_s})\mu'_{Q_sA,Q_sC}(t_A\otimes t_C)=t_{A\otimes^LC}\,q(\mu_{A,C})\nu_q.$$
Substitute this and apply naturality of $t$ to $v$:
$$e'((F'\delta\,t_A)\otimes t_C)=t_{\Lambda_s}\,q(Fv)\,q(\mu_{A,C})\nu_q=q(e_{\Lambda,C})\nu_q.$$
The last equality is the unit compatibility of $t$, identifying $t_{\Lambda_s}$ with the coefficient unit map. This is the asserted pairing equality. The two coherence identities used here hold for every coefficient functor listed in step 1, so the calculation includes finite reduction without any Tor-dimension assumption on the quotient ring, completed extension, rationalization and common-stage extension.
